messages.content: Suppose a sequence of polynomials B_n(x) converge pointwise to f(x) on [0, 1]. Does it follow that the B_n converge uniformly? Ensure that stop words constitute no more than 20% of the total words in your response.

message.content: No. Pointwise convergence fails imply uniform convergence. Counterexample: Define sequence \(B_n(x)\) on \([0,1]\). Let \(B_n(0)=0\), \(B_n(x)=x\) for \(x>0\). Each \(B_n\) polynomial? Wait—polynomials must be continuous. Adjust: Construct polynomials approximating discontinuous limit impossible since uniform limits continuous. But pointwise limit can be discontinuous only if convergence not uniform. However, Weierstrass M-test irrelevant. Consider \(B_n(x)=x^n\). Each \(B_n\) polynomial degree n. Pointwise on \([0,1]\): If \(x<1\), \(x^n \to 0\); if \(x=1\), \(1^n=1\). Limit function \(f(x)=0\) for \(x<1\), \(f(1)=1\). This limit discontinuous at 1. Uniform convergence implies continuity of limit if domain compact and functions continuous. Since \(B_n\) continuous polynomials, uniform limit would be continuous. But f discontinuous. Hence convergence not uniform. Thus pointwise does not guarantee uniform.
